title: Other Desert Cities is playing on Broadway at the Hudson Theatre now ...
transcript: This is one of the starriest plays in New York, with tickets going for over $1,000. And yet I have to question why we even chose to revive this play in the first place. I mean, I can certainly see how it made a big splash in 2011 when it premiered, as the play is pretty critical of the Iraq war, which at that point had been going on for almost a decade. But now, in 2026, so much of that commentary just feels so much less urgent. There are certainly still parallels to be drawn between the conservative family in this play and conservative families today. and the archetypes that these characters inhabit still very much exist, So it doesn't feel completely dated. It just doesn't feel as fresh as it probably did in 2011. But even beyond the timeliness of the piece, I felt the plot was just a bit muddled. because the core of this play is a daughter, played by Lily Rabe, writing a memoir about the death of her brother and is looking for her family's blessing to publish it, despite the fact that it doesn't make them look very good. And while it does take a while to get there, once these discussions get going, it does lead to some really interesting philosophical questions. And this notion around should she publish the novel, should she not? Is not one with a clear answer. However, a lot of these interesting philosophical questions kind of get thrown Out the window with the introduction of a twist towards the end of the show, which obviously I won't spoil, but it is 1) a twist that I kind of saw coming, and 2) just changed the conversation entirely in a way that I found to be far less interesting than the conversation that preceded it. And then, of course, we have the cast, who obviously is the main draw here. Overall, I thought they were good, but didn't really leave much of an impression. Joe Keery, ironically, despite having the smallest role of the five, I thought was really the standout, and I would love to see him do more stage work in the future. But I did feel like Julia Louis Dreyfus and Ed Harris were just a bit out of their depth here. Julia is very much pulling from her Selena Meyer playbook. I just didn't really feel like it worked quite as well for this character. And Ed's performance just felt a little bit uneven to me. He has these really reserved moments contrasted with these really animated moments, and it just never quite connected for me. And this is the issue I think you run into a lot with these celebrity driven plays. They are cast for their box office appeal first and foremost, not necessarily because they are the best actors for the job. And don't get me wrong, they're not bad by any means. They are more than capable actors giving serviceable performances. But When paired with the material, you have okay performances in an okay play that just doesn't quite feel worth the ticket prices that they are charging.
classificationReason: Creator shares direct critical opinions about the Broadway production of Other Desert Cities — questioning the revival's timeliness in 2026, commenting on plot muddling, and specifically naming Lily Rabe's performance. First-hand attendance is clearly implied.
